**Your impact begins here

**As Process Supporter, you will help keep the warehouse for our tablet production running reliably, ensuring stable processes and a high level of quality in our warehouse operations. You will handle deviations and change requests (CR), strengthen processes and make sure solutions work in practice on the shop floor. As the production areas we support grow, your work helps the warehouse deliver more than before and keeps supply moving for people who rely on our treatments.

**What You’ll Bring

**We are looking for a candidate with:

• A bachelor’s degree and relevant experience within production or the pharmaceutical industry.

• Knowledge of GMP and a quality-minded way of working.

• Fluency in English.

• The ability to work independently with support and to be trusted to own your tasks, follow up on agreements and complete work on time.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to build trust with operators, team leaders and colleagues from different disciplines.

• The ability to prioritise in a dynamic environment, communicate status and risks clearly, and escalate in good time.

• Curiosity and a strong desire to learn new skills and adapt to change.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Experience with warehousing, logistics, QC, production or supply chain processes, ideally in a GMP-regulated environment.

• Experience handling deviations, change requests and SOPs, or knowledge of cLEAN/Lean and quality management.

• Experience with validation and qualification.

• Experience with SAP, PAS-X, WMS or comparable systems, and with data tools such as Excel.

We are open to different levels of experience. If you have the right foundations and a strong wish to learn, we can train the rest.

**What You’ll Do

**You will support daily warehouse operations and make sure our processes run reliably. You will solve problems, handle deviations, drive change requests and update work instructions so they reflect how the work is done.

**You Will Also

**

• Prepare for, take part in and present during audits and inspections.

• Improve processes and ways of working, using data to find where the warehouse can optimise and deliver more.

• Help future-proof capacity and flow as the production areas we support continue to grow.

• Share status, risks and learnings clearly, across the organisation and on the shop floor.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Tablet Finished Products (TFP), Manufacturing Area A (MAA), Production Business Support (PBS), Warehouse Support team in Måløv, a team of 10 colleagues: 7 Process Supporters and 3 IT Supporters. The team supports production areas that are experiencing significant growth, including tablet production.

Your closest partners will be operators and team leaders in the warehouse, as well as colleagues in bulk and packaging production, QC, QA, Engineering and Business Support. Together you will keep processes compliant, decisions clear and improvements moving.

This is an on-site role in Måløv. You will be visible on the shop floor, and as a general rule, working from home will not be possible.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will join skilled colleagues in a strong professional environment, with real ownership from the start. We trust you to take responsibility, and we support you with the training and feedback you need to grow in the role.

The warehouse is essential to our success, and the work gives you a chance to uphold quality standards in a setting where they make a daily difference. You will be encouraged to share your perspective, learn new skills and contribute to the team’s results and knowledge sharing.

**Salary

**For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to help the warehouse run with quality and confidence, apply for the Process Supporter role by 8 November 2026.

For further information, please contact Alex Knudsen, Senior Manager at axkd@novonordisk.com.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

You will combine strategic leadership with a hands-on operational approach, ensuring excellence in day-to-day activities while driving long-term growth.

You will work closely with your manager to shape and implement the country strategy, while actively engaging with merchants, airport stakeholders, Customs (SKAT) and your internal teams across both Tax Free and Payment, an area expected to become increasingly important in Denmark over the coming months and years. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a versatile position, balancing commercial development, operational oversight and strategic execution within a Nordic market that demands agility, strong relationships and a strong focus on market-share defence.

**Main Responsibilities

**Your responsibilities will span both strategic and operational dimensions, including:

**Strategic & Business Leadership

**

• Develop, implement and execute business strategies to achieve short- and long-term goals.

• Drive market growth by hunting new merchant partnerships in Payment and farming existing relationships in Tax Free Shopping, defending the established market position.

• Prepare business plans to improve cost-efficiency and operational performance.

• Lead strategy reviews and business development initiatives, identifying opportunities in current and new segments.

**Operational & Team Management

**

• Ensure excellence in airport refund operations, coordinating closely with the Refund Manager and refund agents.

• Support and supervise Key Account Managers in merchant management and sales activities, while maintaining hands-on management of your own merchant portfolio.

• Address day-to-day operational issues with merchants, including IT-related matters.

• Manage hiring, terminations, salary reviews and bonus decisions in alignment with line management.

**Stakeholder Management

**

• Maintain strong relationships with business partners, authorities and key stakeholders, including Customs, airports, merchants, tourism associations and government bodies.

• Negotiate with airport authorities on operational contracts and collaborations.

**Governance & Compliance

**

• Ensure compliance with all relevant laws, rules and company policies.

• Provide monthly reports, market insights and strategic advice to upper management.

• Oversee internal and external communications and key business documentation.

**Every action has an impact. You will make a difference here if:

**

• You thrive in a role that combines strategy with operational involvement and are comfortable getting your hands dirty when needed.

• You bring strong leadership, motivating diverse teams and leading by example.

• You can diagnose business issues quickly and take decisive actions when performance deviates from expectations.

• You build trusted relationships with merchants, institutions and partners, acting as the face of Global Blue in Denmark.

• You can manage multiple business functions simultaneously while keeping strategic priorities clear.

• You bring a dynamic and proactive approach to your work.

**Key competencies to empower your journey.

****You’ll Drive Towards Success If

**

• You demonstrate sharp business judgment, strong analytical skills and the ability to work with business intelligence and big data to identify opportunities.

• You are skilled in negotiation, contract management and partnership development.

• You excel in communication and interpersonal relations, both internally and externally.

• You show excellent organizational and leadership capabilities, including crisis management and decision-making under pressure.

• You have solid financial competencies, being able to use dashboards and reporting systems to drive performance.

• You are proficient in MS Office and used to working with ERP, CRM and financial/reporting systems.

• You are agile and able to make quick decisions, particularly in the fast-moving Payment environment.

• Knowledge of the Point of Sale (POS) IT landscape would be an advantage.

• You have a good understanding of the local Danish retail, merchant and Payment ecosystem.

• Fluent English is required.

Director

CMC Analysis & Characterisation

CMC Analytical Execution & Technology

Location: Måløv

Your impact begins here - **Set the direction. Accelerate delivery. Transform analytical execution.

**Are you a bold and inspiring leader who can turn complexity into clear direction and strong results? As Director of CMC Analytical Execution & Technology (AET), you will lead a multidisciplinary organisation of approximately 150 employees, ensure reliable analytical delivery across a growing development portfolio, and shape the future of automation, digitalisation, and analytical technology. This is an opportunity to combine visible operational leadership with strategic influence - and build the people, partnerships, and capabilities that will advance medicines from development to patients. Apply now and help shape the future of analytical execution.

**What You’ll Do

**As Director for CMC AET, you will lead a multi-disciplinary area consisting of five operational analytical teams, one IT team, and one Technology Engineering team. Together, these teams are responsible for delivering analytical results across the entire development project portfolio, while driving digitalization, automation, and technology advancement across the area. You will ensure reliable, compliant, and efficient operations through strong leadership, clear prioritization, robust resource planning, and close collaboration with key stakeholders.

At the same time, you will define and execute the strategic roadmap for analytical execution, digital capabilities, and technology innovation, ensuring scalable solutions and future-ready capabilities that support an expanding portfolio and increasing business complexity.

**Your Key Responsibilities Will Be

**

• Lead people and organisational capability: set a clear direction, develop leaders and talents, and build a high-performing organisation with the capabilities required to support current and future business needs.

• Drive performance and execution excellence: ensure reliable, compliant, and timely analytical delivery through strong operational leadership, clear accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement.

• Set strategic direction: define and drive the long-term strategy for analytical execution, validation, release readiness, and technology enablement, balancing business priorities, future capability needs, and regulatory expectations.

• Lead and build strategic partnerships: establish trusted stakeholder relations across the value chain and create alignment around priorities, capacity, risks, and resource investments to enable successful portfolio delivery.

• Shape the future through technology and innovation: define the vision and strategic direction for automation, digitalisation, and future ways of working across AnaC. Influence organisational priorities and investments to build the capabilities needed to meet future portfolio and business demands.

Your success requires a visible, hands-on operational leadership profile combined with strong strategic judgement. You stay close to execution performance, use KPIs and lead-time data to drive action, identify risks and constraints early, and work proactively with stakeholders to remove barriers and protect delivery. With full decision authority, you set objectives with significant functional impact and take accountability for people decisions, operational performance, strategic capability development, and successful project transfers from Research to Global Manufacturing & Supply.

You report to the Vice President (VP) of CMC Analysis & Characterisation (AnaC) and will be part of the leadership team in AnaC.

**Who You’ll Work With

**CMC AnaC is responsible for analytical development, characterisation, bioanalysis, stability, comparability, validation, release and lifecycle analytical support across Novo's product portfolio.

CMC AET consists of approximately 150 employees in Måløv, organised across five execution teams responsible for validation and QC/release testing, as well as a technology team and an IT team. The department is accountable for strong day-to-day analytical execution, predictable delivery, and transparent performance management, while strategically developing the automation, digital solutions, technologies, and capabilities required for the future analytical landscape.

We offer a dynamic and fast-paced environment where operational excellence, innovation, and collaboration go hand in hand. We take ownership, challenge the status quo, and are committed to delivering high-quality analytical support to patients and the business.

**What You’ll Bring

**We are looking for a seasoned and self‑motivated leader who thrives on taking initiative and ownership. You bring:

• An MSc (minimum) and + 5 years of relevant experience, with significant experience within QC, analytical development or other relevant CMC or Product Supply disciplines.

• + 5 years of proven leadership experience with the ability to lead multi‑disciplinary teams and deliver results at a strategic level. Senior leadership experience is a requirement.

• Broad cross‑functional experience within CMC Development, with strong organisational understanding and the ability to influence at VP level.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to present complex scientific and strategic topics to senior management.

• A demonstrated track record of driving change, challenging the status quo, and improving business outcomes.

• A strong Lean mindset and experience applying continuous improvement principles to simplify workflows, reduce lead times, improve capacity utilisation and build sustainable operational performance.

You lead with confidence, energy, and trust, creating clarity in complexity and belief in times of uncertainty. You set a strong tone of ownership and optimism - “we’ve got this” - and lead in line with Novo leadership behaviours by delivering on commitments, developing others, challenging constructively, and making decisions for the greater good.

**What You Can Expect Here

**At Novo, you can expect a role where your scientific judgement matters, your ideas are listened to, and your work helps move complex development projects forward. You will have opportunities to deepen your expertise, build cross-functional influence and grow in a collaborative environment where initiative is encouraged. You will be supported to perform at your best and trusted to take ownership, while contributing to work that helps create progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short‑term and/or long‑term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Due to short deadline please apply as fast as possible.

**For further information, please contact VP CMC AnaC, Kristine Buch Uldahl, at kbuu@novonordisk.com

**About ALK

**ALK is a global pharmaceutical company specializing in allergy immunotherapy. We are driven by a high level of professionalism, integrity, an open-minded approach and contributing to an inspiring and fun working environment together with our colleagues. We provide an attractive working environment for individuals looking for both personal and professional development. You will be part of an engaged and informal team who values skill and knowledge creation.

**The position

**ALK is looking for a strategic and experienced Director, Finance Digital Transformation, to lead the contribution from Finance’s to the SAP S/4HANA transformation and drive the continuous development of ALK’s Finance application landscape.

In this role, you will ensure that finance requirements, controls, data integrity, and reporting needs are embedded in the future ERP landscape. You will also lead the roadmap for SAP, BW/BI, AI, and automation initiatives while building a centre of excellence for finance applications and projects.

As the primary interface between Finance, Global Business IT (GBIT), and external implementation partners, you will play a key role in shaping how technology enables Finance across ALK.

**Responsibilities

**

• Lead the Finance workstream in the SAP S/4HANA transformation from requirements and design through testing, cutover, and hypercare.

• Represent Finance in programme governance and manage finance-related risks, decisions, controls, data migration, and reporting requirements.

• Develop and maintain Finance’s application and technology strategy in cooperation with the Global Finance Board.

• Lead, develop, and motivate a team of 3–5 finance application and project specialists.

• Oversee the operation, maintenance, improvement, and governance of core finance applications, including SAP, BW/BI, and related finance systems.

• Identify and lead opportunities involving AI, automation, advanced analytics, and self-service reporting.

• Manage the Finance IT project portfolio, including prioritisation, resourcing, delivery, and status reporting.

• Coordinate system releases, upgrades, testing, access management, documentation, training, and user support.

• Ensure appropriate finance master data management and coordinate Finance IT audit deliverables.

• Act as the primary Finance partner to GBIT, SAP implementation partners, technology vendors, and external consultants.

**Experience And Qualifications

**

• Master’s degree in Finance, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field.

• At least 8 years of experience in finance systems, finance IT, or related roles.

• Hands-on experience with SAP finance modules; experience with SAP S/4HANA is strongly preferred.

• Experience leading or playing a senior role in a major ERP transformation.

• Knowledge of BW/BI platforms and finance reporting or planning solutions.

• Experience with AI, automation, or advanced analytics in a finance context is an advantage.

• Proven people leadership experience, preferably managing a team of specialists.

• Strong project and programme management skills; relevant certification such as PMP or PRINCE2 is an advantage.

• Strong understanding of finance systems integration, governance, controls, and data management.

• Excellent stakeholder management, influencing, communication, and negotiation skills.

• Structured, analytical, and process-oriented approach with a strong focus on continuous improvement.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

**We Offer

**ALK provides a dynamic and accommodating work environment, complete with inspiring and challenging assignments. You are able to actively influence and challenge the status quo. Our flat structures attract independent individuals who like to feel the progress of the business and enjoy being close to the decision-making process. We consider our pioneering spirit, coupled with our trustworthiness, our winning formula.

**_Denmark

_**Our offices in Denmark offer a green view of the DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We believe that physical presence enforces strong teamwork and collaboration and creates success, so it is important that you enjoy coming to work at our site with a degree of flexibility to also work from home.

**_Poland

_**ALK GBSC offers a safe and healthy workspace in a modern office (Aleja Pokoju 1) that features the best of Danish design, including an open floorplan, wooden flooring, stand-up desks, a chill-out room and a fully equipped kitchen with the best view in Kraków.

Join us at ALK and be a part of an organization that values integrity, innovation, and making a difference in the lives of those we serve.

Allergy impacts and challenges the lives of millions of adults and children every day. At ALK, our purpose is to improve the lives of people living with allergies. Building on our strong heritage, we are guided by our strategy, Allergy+, that shows us a clear path towards this goal through focus, innovation, cultivation and optimisation.

Read more about our corporate strategy and our ambitions for growth

**Fair and unbiased recruitment at ALK

**At ALK, we believe that every candidate deserves to be evaluated fairly and respectfully. Our recruitment process is designed to give each applicant an equal opportunity, regardless of their background. Read more about fair and unbiased recruitment at ALK.

If you are applying from North America, please know that we are committed to fair, unbiased and non-discriminatory recruitment practices and to complying with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws. Employment decisions are made based on qualifications, skills and experience, without discrimination on the basis of legally protected characteristics. For more information, please visit the official websites of the relevant authorities: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP).

**Your recruitment journey at ALK

**Curious to learn more about our recruitment process? Please visit this page.

**The position

**You will join Omnigame’s Legal & Compliance Department and work closely with the Head of Regulatory Affairs & Compliance. Your primary focus will be regulatory compliance relating to Omnigame’s B2C operations, specifically its Danish-licensed online casino activities and, as relevant, future B2C markets.

In this role, you will support the day-to-day management of regulatory requirements applicable to Omnigame’s B2C operations, ensuring that regulatory obligations are identified, implemented and appropriately documented across the business. You will work closely with relevant stakeholders across the organization, including Safer Gambling, AML, Technology and Commercial.

As Omnigame continues to develop its business and enter new markets, the role will provide opportunities to participate in regulatory projects, licence applications and the implementation of new regulatory requirements.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Maintain expert and up-to-date knowledge of legislation, regulations, licence conditions, regulatory guidance and technical requirements applicable to Omnigame’s B2C gambling operations.

• Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on Omnigame’s B2C activities, ensuring that relevant requirements are communicated to and implemented by the appropriate business functions.

• Support the business on day-to-day B2C regulatory compliance matters and provide practical guidance on the interpretation and implementation of regulatory requirements.

• Coordinate and support regulatory reporting, notifications and other submissions to relevant gambling authorities.

• Support the maintenance of Omnigame’s existing B2C gambling licences and assist with applications for licences in new jurisdictions.

• Support regulatory implementation projects, including changes to products, platforms, games, suppliers and operational processes.

• Draft, review and maintain regulatory policies, procedures, controls and internal guidance relevant to Omnigame’s B2C operations.

• Monitor compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and identify regulatory risks, deficiencies and areas for improvement.

• Recommend appropriate remediation measures and coordinate their implementation with relevant stakeholders.

• Work closely with the Safer Gambling and AML teams to ensure that regulatory developments and operational changes are appropriately reflected in Omnigame’s safer gambling, AML/CFT, sanctions and player-protection framework.

• Coordinate and support regulatory inspections, audits, information requests and other interactions with gambling authorities.

• Maintain appropriate regulatory documentation, evidence, registers and compliance records.

• Provide regulatory input into new products, features and business initiatives and participate in relevant cross-functional projects.

• Develop and deliver regulatory training and guidance to relevant stakeholders where required.

• Support the Head of Regulatory Affairs & Compliance and Chief Legal & Compliance Officer on B2C regulatory and compliance projects.

**Qualifications And Experience

**

• A relevant higher education degree within law, business law, compliance, governance, risk management or a comparable field.

• Approximately 3–5 years’ relevant experience, preferably from the gambling sector; experience from another highly regulated sector, audit, consultancy, risk or compliance may also be relevant.

• Experience with regulatory compliance within online gambling or another highly regulated industry, with B2C gambling regulation being a particular advantage.

• Experience interpreting regulatory requirements and translating them into practical operational requirements, controls and procedures.

• Experience with regulatory reporting, licence applications and/or regulatory change management is an advantage.

• Ability to draft and maintain clear company policies and operational procedures.

• High degree of integrity, initiative, attention to detail and ability to work effectively in time-sensitive situations.

• Fluency in English, both spoken and written, with strong communication skills.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively across functions and seniority levels.

**Bonus Skills

**

• Knowledge of auditing principles and practices.

• Knowledge of data governance and data protection principles.

• Experience providing specialized regulatory or compliance training.

• Additional language skills.

****Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and the application deadline is 9 November 2026.

We are looking for a CRM & Lifecycle Manager to join Hårklinikken as we continue to develop and grow our global ecommerce business.

We operate six Shopify sites across the US, UK, EU, Denmark, Iceland and the UAE, with the US representing our largest growth market and subscriptions playing a central role in our model.

You will own the CRM and lifecycle journey across our markets, building the communication, flows and experiences that help turn first-time clients into long-term relationships. From onboarding and treatment support to subscriptions, repeat purchase, loyalty and win-back, you will help clients stay engaged, consistent and cared for throughout their journey with us.

Working hands-on in Klaviyo and Recharge, you will use data and customer insights to understand where clients engage, where they drop off and what helps them stay. You will continuously test and improve the lifecycle journey, with a particular focus on the first 90 days and subscription retention.

Success in this role means improving 90-day retention, increasing the number of subscribers who stay for at least three deliveries, strengthening repeat purchase rates and growing CRM revenue across markets.

You will track cohorts and LTV by market and share what you learn, helping those insights shape our wider acquisition and ecommerce activities.

Primary Relationships

You will report to the Global Director of Ecommerce and work closely with the Senior Ecommerce Manager as part of our ecommerce team in Copenhagen.

You will also collaborate closely with Brand, our clinics and our Client Care Teams, particularly around campaigns, the client journey, loyalty and client feedback.

You will work closely with our Content Marketing Manager, providing clear briefs for CRM campaigns and customer communications.

Key Responsibilities

• Klaviyo. Build and run flows, segments, campaigns and SMS across six markets, working with our Content Marketing Manager who develops copy from your briefs.

• The first 90 days. Own the onboarding journey for new clients, helping them start their treatment right and stay with it.

• Subscriptions in Recharge. Manage sign-ups, retention, churn and win-back, testing what helps subscribers stay longer.

• Consultation to treatment. Develop booking reminders and post-consultation flows that help turn consultations into lasting treatments, both in our clinics and at home.

• Loyalty, reviews and client feedback. Work closely with our Client Care Team to understand where clients get stuck and what brings them back.

• The campaign calendar. Coordinate the campaign calendar so CRM, the site and paid media go live at the same time with the same message.

Core Competencies

This role requires strong CRM and lifecycle experience combined with a hands-on, structured and analytical approach. You are comfortable working with data, understanding customer behaviour and turning insights into actions that strengthen retention.

You keep many moving parts on track and care about the client, not just the open rate. You understand how to grow retention through value rather than discounts, and you know when one email is one too many. You don't need to tick every box to be the right fit. We would love to hear from you if you bring strong CRM or lifecycle experience, a customer-focused mindset, a genuine interest in building relationships that last and supporting our mission

What You Bring:

• 3-5 years of experience in CRM, retention or lifecycle marketing, ideally within DTC ecommerce.

• Strong hands-on Klaviyo skills, with experience building flows, segments and templates yourself.

• Experience with subscriptions, ideally Recharge.

• A track record of delivering results that you can demonstrate through data.

• Confidence working with data, with the ability to read a cohort and understand what to test next.

• Fluent English.

It is an advantage if you also have:

• Experience working across several markets or Shopify storefronts, ideally including the US.

• Experience with a premium beauty, wellness or personal care brand with a regimen or subscription model.

• Experience with loyalty or review platforms.

• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language.

Who Are We?

Founded in 1992 in Copenhagen, Hårklinikken is a leading scalp and hair health clinic with more than 30 years of experience. We help clients achieve optimal scalp health and long-lasting hair gain, combining expert guidance with clean and gentle products formulated to support healthy hair growth.

Our approach began with Hårklinikken’s founder and lead researcher, Lars Skjøth, who developed a diagnostic, consultation-based approach centred around understanding each client’s individual scalp and hair needs. Today, The Hårklinikken Method brings together decades of expertise with the personalised care that has been at the heart of Hårklinikken from the beginning.

Clients come to us in different ways, whether through a consultation or by discovering and purchasing our products online. Through virtual consultations or in person at our clinics in New York, Beverly Hills, Copenhagen, Aarhus, Dubai and Reykjavik, our Hair Specialists combine their expertise with an individual assessment of each client’s scalp, hair, lifestyle and environment to create a personalised regimen designed around their specific needs.

However their journey begins, we are here to guide and support our clients along the way. From helping them find what is right for their individual needs to supporting them in achieving the best possible results, we want every client to feel confident, understood and cared for throughout their Hårklinikken journey.

We’re on a mission to help as many people as possible achieve fuller, stronger, healthier hair with products that are powered by science, perfected by experts and proven by over 100,000 clients.

What We Offer

• A new team, where you shape how we work from day one.

• Full ownership of CRM and subscriptions across six markets.

• Short decision paths in an owner-led company.

• Close collaboration with our clinics, where the treatment starts.

• A real work-life balance, with flexibility in how you plan your day.

• An international team and modern clinics with a strong focus on quality and aesthetics.

• Growth opportunities in a safe work environment.

• Pension, holiday allowance and discounts on our products and treatments.

The role reports to the Global Director of Ecommerce and is based on site in Copenhagen. It is a permanent, full-time position, starting as soon as possible and ideally no later than 1 March 2027.

jobs.description:
Supply Chain Launch Manager for global launch projects

Would you like to help orchestrate the global launch of new products, representing our supply chain throughout the entire launch projects?

Join a global group of skilled supply chain professionals and follow new products from early development all the way to market – as your input will ensure that we deliver the best products to people with intimate healthcare needs.

“WE play a key part in planning and executing successful launches – and we are a valued voice in the process, allowing us to set a clear direction,” explains Head of Supply Chain Launch, Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen.

Join our highly experienced Launch department

Together, we are 7 colleagues, responsible for supply chain activities related to bringing new and innovative products to market within Chronic Care and Wound Care products. A good part of our time, we spend working with our factories in Hungary, Costa Rica, and soon Portugal.

“As we are each dedicated to different projects, discussing what we’ve learned with each other is very important to us. And we’ll be there to make sure you get to ease into the position,” says Daniel.

Ensure that supply chain is covered in every project

As part of the Coloplast global supply chain, you will find yourself in the middle of a web of stakeholders working towards launching new Chronic Care and Wound Care products. Here, you will be dedicated to specific projects, acting as supply chain lead or subject matter expert, representing the voice of supply chain and making sure supply chain is on track for launch.

Specifically, you will be the subject matter expert from supply chain, staying up to date on project progression. Moreover, you will plan the launch and make sure that systems, manufacturing, stock levels, etc. are ready for launch. And when you meet a bump in the road, you will figure out solutions with the project team.

From early project development until post-launch, you will:

•    Influence project decisions and direction early, to avoid supply chain risks

•    Drive the supply chain plan with manufacturing sites, balancing project deliverables and commercial considerations to launch on time

•    Produce launch scenarios in collaboration with other departments and ensure alignment with the rest of the organization

•    Coordinate activities at our production sites and flag supply chain risks

•    Make sure systems, such as planning, base data and distribution, are ready for launch

•    Follow up on delivery performance of newly launched items after launch

Your work may take you traveling roughly 2 weeks per year, primarily to our factory in Hungary. However, you will have a say on how the trips are planned, so they will fit with the rest of your life.

Supply chain knowledge and stakeholder management skills

In this role, you must be able to work cross-functionally, using your good stakeholder management skills to incorporate a wide range of input from across the business. Also, you can work with limited supervision in your projects, representing the voice of supply chain, making decisions, and setting a direction for your area.

Finally, we imagine that you:

•    Have a degree in supply chain or engineering

•    Have some experience, either within supply chain or logistics and a good conception of production processes

•    Possibly have some experience working in projects, allowing you to consider both commercial and supply chain perspectives

•    Are good at Excel and at adapting to new systems

•    Are fluent in English

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please reach out to Head of Supply Chain Launch,

Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen on DKDAAR@coloplast.com. We will take candidates into the recruitment process continuously, so do not hesitate to apply. This position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

Visit us on Coloplast.com.

Watch the film. Follow us on LinkedIn.

Do you want to help shape the next generation of AI-powered business capabilities and are you motivated by turning business opportunities into intelligent agentic products?

“At Arla, we are scaling proven Data Science and Machine Learning capabilities into business-critical products that support commercial decisions across our markets. We are looking for someone who can combine strong quantitative modelling skills with modern software and AI engineering practices to help drive this journey.” says Andreas Therkildsen, Manager, IT Product Architect.

How you will make an impact

You will join a dedicated product team responsible for the Net Revenue Management (NRM) Commercial Intelligence Platform and its growing portfolio of pricing, promotion, forecasting, and AI-enabled capabilities. Working closely with commercial stakeholders, product owners, architects, engineers, and data specialists, you will:

• Build a deep understanding of pricing, promotions, demand drivers, and commercial decision-making within Net Revenue Management.

• Design and develop statistical, econometric, and machine learning models that generate actionable business insights.

• Apply Machine Learning models and inference techniques to evaluate commercial initiatives and identify revenue opportunities, and understand why the models perform as they do.

This position is based in Aarhus, Denmark or Gdańsk, Poland, with an expectation of 50% office presence. Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Commercial Excellence & Commercial Strategy
jobs.description:
Do you thrive at the intersection between commercial strategy, transformation and execution. Do you enjoy setting the direction and then rolling up your sleeves to make it happen? Join 3Shape’s CCO Leadership Team and shape how a global MedTech leader grows. We are looking for someone who isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo and brings a healthy disruptive edge to how things are done.

About 3Shape

3Shape started with a simple idea: to make 3D scanning better. We applied it first to the hearing industry and then to dentistry, and today our scanning and CAD/CAM solutions help dental and hearing professionals treat more people, more effectively. Every second of every day, a 3Shape scanner is in use somewhere in the world. We are 2,200+ colleagues of 45+ nationalities, headquartered in central Copenhagen at Kongens Nytorv.

Our commercial organisation is approximately 1,000 people strong and delivers our products to customers in 29 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia. Our flagship products include a mixture of hardware and software; TRIOS intraoral scanners, the Dental System CAD software and the 3Shape Unite platform.

Your new role

As Senior Director, Commercial Excellence & Commercial Strategy, you report directly to our SVP of Commercial (CCO) and act as a close sparring partner. You sit on the CCO Leadership Team with the leaders of Global Customer Success, Global Marketing and our three Regional VPs, and you lead a team of Commercial Excellence Managers, transformation agents, project managers and data and reporting specialists.

You own the commercial strategy for Dental Clinics, DSOs (dental service organisations) and Laboratories, and you build Commercial Excellence into a global function that turns strategic choices into growth across markets.

Leading leaders and running Commercial Excellence should come naturally to you. The real stretch in this role is driving a transformation and professionalization of the commercial organization with the aim of lifting topline growth.

You will work side by side with colleagues at our Copenhagen headquarters in Denmark, in an office-based role, and you will regularly travel to spend time with our great people in local sales hubs and meet customers at leading dental events around the world.

What you will do

Commercial strategy & transformation

• Own the three-year commercial strategy and the annual commercial strategy cycle, linked to budget, targets and business plans.

• Turn the strategy into a roadmap with clear owners, milestones and KPIs, and keep execution on track.

• Lead the CCO transformation portfolio and challenge how we get most impact across segments, markets, channels and new offerings.

• Build alignment across global functions, regions and markets, including through our Country Manager forum.

Commercial Excellence

• Define and scale the global Commercial Excellence operating model, from customer potential and territory management to sales plays and tools.

• Turn market, customer and competitor insight into decision-ready recommendations for the CCO Leadership Team.

• Set the CRM standard and the commercial performance framework together with IT, Data Management and Financial Planning & BI.

• Partner with Finance and Portfolio and Product Strategy (PPS) on pricing and discount governance, and enable go-to-market for new offerings.

• Drive launch excellence for new products and offerings, with a repeatable launch playbook, clear market readiness criteria and adoption KPIs that get new solutions into customers’ hands quickly across all markets.

What success looks like

• A three-year commercial strategy with clear priorities agreed in the CCO Leadership Team and linked to budget and targets.

• Commercial transformation delivering tangible impact with revenue growth, efficiency gains and capability uplift in priority markets, with learnings carried into the rest.

• Commercial Excellence established as a recognised discipline, with a strong team and a clear role across Commercial, Portfolio and Product Strategy (PPS) and Finance.

• CRM adopted to standard in all markets, and leadership decisions taken on a shared, current picture of market, customers and competitors.

• A proven launch excellence model in place, with new offerings reaching target adoption faster across markets.

Who you are

You are an experienced senior commercial leader with documented results from comparable roles. You hold a master’s degree in economics, business or similar, and you bring:

• Experience leading leaders and engaging, inspiring and developing people.

• A track record of owning and driving commercial strategy from within the business, rather than as an external advisor, with measurable results to show for it.

• Deep Commercial Excellence experience, including shaping and growing the function in a fast-growing organisation. MedTech experience is a plus.

• Experience leading complex, cross-functional transformations with executive stakeholders.

• Executive presence and the courage to challenge senior leaders and established ways of working.

• International experience from a global matrix organisation.

What 3Shape offers

• Real influence on how a global MedTech leader grows, a premium brand guided by innovation and customer focus.

• A strategic mandate across regions to shape our global commercial approach, with real room to influence and make decisions.

• A seat on the CCO Leadership Team and high visibility with senior leaders across 3Shape.

• A role as the CCO’s personal sparring partner on the commercial path forward.

• Global scale and impact across 29 countries, and the opportunity to lead a strong, international team.

• An attractive healthcare package, daily breakfast and lunch from our own chefs, and plenty of social clubs and activities.

• Modern offices in central Copenhagen, near Kongens Nytorv and Nyhavn.

Application process

• To apply, click "Apply now" and attach your CV including a short motivation in one document.

• Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

Apylon is building the intelligent revenue management platform for European healthcare. Billions of euros flow between hospitals and insurers through fragmented, manual workflows — a maze of rules, conditions and requirements.

We believe this is a machine learning and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe.

As a Founders Associate, you’ll work directly with the founding team on the highest-priority challenges facing the company. This is a unique opportunity to gain exposure to all aspects of building a venture-backed startup — from strategy and operations to customer success and fundraising.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

• Building and improving internal processes and operations as we scale.

• Supporting fundraising efforts — preparing materials, coordinating with investors, and managing due diligence.

• Highly organized with excellent attention to detail.

What Apylon offers

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code - powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue operations.

The successful candidate will play an important role in maintaining product quality, driving process improvements, and supporting production through strong quality leadership.

• A strong communicator with excellent collaboration skills.

• Results driven with a continuous improvement mindset.

• Capable of balancing strategic initiatives with day-to-day operational responsibilities.

**

• An exciting opportunity to shape and improve our quality processes.

We're reshaping how Product and Tech work at PriceShape, and you'll help build it. You'll join a small product team that owns its part of the product end to end. You'll ship to production every day, in small steps, behind feature toggles. You'll build with agents from your first week. And underneath it all is a genuinely hard problem. We collect and match pricing data from across the web, and it has to be complete, correct and fresh enough for our customers to act on it.

While agents write most of the code, we rely on senior human judgment and evaluation. If you want to be part of improving our product and our speed of learning, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

You'll be a developer in one of our product teams, working in a small team with one or two other developers, a product manager, a designer and a tech lead.

Your team owns its part of the product, all the way from the customer problem to the service running in production. You'll build it, ship it and run it, together with the rest of the team. Developers here are part of finding the solution, not a step after it has been decided.

Not all of this is in place yet. Some of it you'll find working well, and some of it you'll help us build. Some people here have done a lot of this before, but we're all still learning better ways.

You can work on-site in our Aarhus HQ or remotely from the EU or the UK. English is our working language, and the team is international.

Shaping solutions with your team

• 
You'll hear customer problems first hand, often enough to make good product and technical calls without asking.

• 
You'll bring technical options, costs and what has recently become possible into the conversation early. We explore more than one solution for every problem.

• 
You'll cut the work so the riskiest assumption reaches production first. Nothing we plan should take more than a week to reach production.

Building and shipping

• 
You'll ship small changes to production continuously. We work trunk based with feature toggles, and roll changes out gradually so they can be turned off without a new deploy.

• 
You'll write the tests as part of the change. There is no test phase and no one else whose job is to find your bugs.

• 
You'll watch how each change behaves in production and improve it in the next deploy when the evidence says so.

• 
You'll change infrastructure through code, the same way you change everything else.

Building with agents

• 
Claude Code is rolled out across the engineering team, and agents are a normal part of how we build.

• 
Most of the detailed decisions in a working day are yours. You make them in a tight loop with an agent, guided by your team's documented product principles, design system and technical decisions. When something falls outside them, you pull in the right person.

• 
You'll keep the context in your repositories current, so the next developer or agent starts from how the code actually works.

• 
You're responsible for what an agent produces in the same way as for code you wrote by hand.

Running what you build

• 
Your team runs its part of the product in production, including availability, scalability, security and bugs. You'll be part of that, including when something breaks.

• 
You'll make sure problems show up in monitoring before customers notice them.

• 
You'll keep dependencies current and fix small issues as they appear, a day at a time, rather than saving them up for a big project.

Working toward outcomes

• 
Your team works toward outcomes, and you'll know which outcome your work serves and whether it moved.

• 
Work is done when the outcome moved or when we decided to stop. When we stop, we stop cleanly, with nothing half built left behind.
